concepts.title: Midnight Beach: Masked Player vs. Skeleton
concepts.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: revised widescreen Last Chance Resort volleyball game concept, landscape 16:10.
Input images: Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, the earlier beach game concept. Images 2–5 are STYLE REFERENCES supplied by the user: bold ink-mask portrait, vintage slasher comic, black stippled hooded skulls, and purple/mint fantasy horror comic. Borrow their print language and visual character vocabulary; do not reproduce their exact panels, combat poses, or copyrighted character identities.
Primary request: redraw the ENTIRE target as a flat, hand-inked vintage horror comic / screen-printed poster, and completely redesign BOTH playable characters as horror characters. This must be a decisive artistic transformation of characters AND environment.
Scene: same moonlit tropical beach and distant right-hand hotel, jagged palms, moon and black cloud shapes. Preserve the recognizable side-view arena layout, horizon, two extreme boundary walls with service buttons, continuous horizontal court, single narrow central net pole viewed edge-on, one airborne volleyball, two gift-delivery quadcopters, left magnet robot, right boxing-glove robot. Simplify background detail into bold graphic shapes.
Left player: an ORIGINAL tall masked horror figure leaping to return the volleyball. Wide-brimmed battered ochre hat, cropped fluttering coat with worn cuffs, indigo cloth face covering with a simple asymmetric black ink-stain pattern, ochre gloves, dark plum trousers and boots. Unmistakable covered face and costume, with clear separated articulated arms and bent legs. His raised hand strikes the ball; empty hands, no weapons.
Right player: a FULL SKELETON volleyball opponent with a prominent bone-white skull, dark eye sockets, readable rib cage, spine, thin articulated arms and legs, torn plum athletic shorts and wrist wraps. Athletic braced ragdoll pose, skeleton hands ready to receive. Bones must read clearly against a darker calm background; no living human face or muscular skin torso.
Style: exactly the broad print qualities in the user's references: thick irregular black outlines, large solid black shadow areas, vigorous angular hatching, limited FLAT spot-color shapes, coarse halftone dots, slightly misregistered ink, weathered paper / screen-print grain. Use muted periwinkle blue, violet-plum, pale mint, aged bone-cream and sparing ochre. Poster-like contrast, stylized graphic anatomy and expressive crooked poses. Moon is a simple aged cream disc. Ocean uses a few jagged ink bands. Robots and drones must also become drawn comic objects, not remaining CGI cutouts.
Composition invariants: one coherent landscape image, exactly TWO full-body players on opposite sides; preserve floor line, central pole and left/right gameplay zones. Players around 25–30% of frame height, equipment spatially separate. Keep ball easy to find and the playing floor unobstructed.
Avoid: all glossy CGI, 3D rendering, photorealistic flesh, smooth gradients, realistic cinematic bloom, volumetric fog, airbrushed shading, extra human spectators, floating giant portraits, collage panels, text, HUD, speech bubbles, logos, watermark, blood, gore, knives, guns. Opaque background.

concepts.title: Sealed Arena: Hooded Skeleton vs. Werewolf
concepts.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: revised widescreen Last Chance Resort volleyball game concept, landscape 16:10.
Input images: Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, the earlier indoor arena concept. Images 2–5 are STYLE REFERENCES supplied by the user: bold ink-mask portrait, vintage slasher comic, black stippled hooded skulls, and purple/mint fantasy horror comic. Images 4 and 5 especially inform the hooded skeleton and feral creature shapes. Use their style, not their existing composition.
Primary request: fully redraw the target in bold vintage horror-comic ink and replace BOTH human tourist players with a hooded skeletal player and an anthropomorphic werewolf player. Make the characters immediately unlike the earlier human athletes.
Scene: same enclosed domed resort sports hall, curved heavy architectural ribs, tall dark windows with tropical silhouettes outside, readable straight horizontal court and boundary walls. Retain the one thin center net pole viewed edge-on, one airborne volleyball, two gift-carrying quadcopters, left exposed-coil spring machine, right wheeled luggage porter. Rebuild everything as a cohesive flat ink illustration. Ceiling and windows form large ominous black masses with a few pale mint and purple graphic light strips. Floor reflections are broken flat ink shapes.
Left player: an original HOODED SKELETON, aged bone-white skull with unmistakable hollow eye sockets inside a torn dark-violet hood, rib cage visible through an open cropped cloak, thin ivory bony arms and legs, simple torn shorts. Flailing backward in midair above the exposed spring machine, clearly articulated ragdoll skeleton anatomy, skull facing the ball. Short cloak preserves the silhouette of the limbs.
Right player: an original upright WEREWOLF volleyball opponent, angular snarling mint-green muzzle, jagged purple mane, black shadowed furry torso, lean long arms with clawed hands, bent digitigrade legs, torn purple sport shorts. Reaching upward to hit the volleyball with a large open clawed hand, athletic awkward airborne pose, no weapons. Full body readable and separated from the porter.
Style and palette: same vintage printed horror comic language as the attached references: chunky uneven black contours, dense black silhouettes, sharp scratchy hatching, coarse stippling and halftone, flat dusty periwinkle / violet and acidic pale mint against deep black, bone-cream skull highlights, tiny muted coral accent lights. Visible paper and worn ink texture. Bold two-dimensional graphic form and aggressive cartoon anatomy, no photographic or sculpted shading. Draw machines with the same black contours and flat colors.
Composition invariants: keep the target's side-on court framing and main object locations. Exactly TWO full-body horror players on opposite sides, about 25–30% of frame height; keep the center gap, ball path, pole and grounded equipment legible. One unified landscape frame, no comic panels.
Avoid: glossy 3D, photorealistic people, unchanged human faces or skin bodies, smooth gradients, realistic volumetric lighting, airbrush painting, giant skulls floating in background, extra characters, text, HUD, speech bubbles, logos, watermark, blood, gore, swords, knives or firearms. Opaque background.
